name: Clay surface
oneLine: A mineral surface that holds nucleotides still so they can link.
howItWorks: Clay sheets carry a charge that grabs nucleotides. Held side by side, the letters join into short chains. Floating free, they rarely would.
deeper: In the 1990s and 2000s James Ferris showed a clay called montmorillonite links activated nucleotides into chains up to about 50 letters.
sizeComparison: a 100,000th the width of a hair
simplification: The chains snap on much faster than in real life.
